beats.text: You don't need to warm up your car for five minutes.
That advice comes from old carburetor cars. Cold fuel didn't turn to vapor well, so they ran rough.
Modern engines use sensors to meter the fuel, so they run fine right away.
Oil reaches the engine parts in seconds.
About thirty seconds is plenty. Then drive gently.
Idling gets zero miles per gallon, and the engine warms up slower than when you drive.
So skip the wait. Just go, gently.
